title: Tangents and the context budget
hook: Branch a side-conversation, then come back exactly where you were.

back.lead: A tangent branches into a side-conversation that inherits the full conversation history, lets you explore freely, then returns you to exactly where you left off. Alongside it, the context command reports a per-tool token breakdown, so what is consuming the context window is visible rather than inferred.

kv.v: Not a new session and not a fork you have to reconcile. It inherits the history, so the detour has the same context, and abandoning it costs nothing.
A per-tool breakdown attributes context consumption to the tool responsible. A single verbose MCP server can dominate a window, and without attribution that looks like the model losing track.
Context is a budget, and the expensive mistake is spending it on an exploratory question that then crowds out the work. A tangent makes the detour cheap; the breakdown makes the spend legible.

back.hookline: Context is a budget. A tangent is how you spend some of it without losing your place.
